A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CADmium study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and added discussion.

before.justification: v2 reports original annotation-quality analyses, CAD-generation evaluations, model-size ablations, and common-subset results in Figure 2 and Tables 1–8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and reports expanded annotation comparisons using CADLLM and two LLM judges, plus qualitative preliminary fine-tuning findings.

M1.justification: The GPT-4.1 annotation pipeline, minimal-JSON representation, Qwen2.5-Coder LoRA fine-tuning, training objective, and greedy generation procedure remain unchanged. Appendix E explains existing choices rather than introducing a revised method.

E1.justification: The CAD-generation coverage remains DeepCAD/CADmium, Text2CAD, CADPrompt, and Fusion360. CADLLM supplies alternative expert annotations for corresponding CAD objects in the comparison; no additional CAD domain, represented object population, or generation task is established.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds CADLLM as an evaluated annotation comparator alongside Text2CAD. The CAD-generation comparator configurations in Tables 1–8 remain unchanged; newly discussed CADFusion and CAD-Coder are not added as evaluated generation baselines.

E3.justification: Annotation judging changes from 10,000 pairs evaluated by Gemma-3 12B to 10,000 three-annotation groups evaluated by Gemma-3 12B and Mistral Small 3.2 24B. Appendix C updates response labels accordingly. Generation splits, budgets, and reconstruction evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The second judge extends assessment across evaluator families. Appendix E newly reports qualitative comparisons involving LoRA ranks 8 and 16 and full fine-tuning. Existing model-scale ablations, common-subset analyses, and geometric failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same single-run, test-sample confidence intervals, paired and unpaired hypothesis tests, and Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Adding another judge does not introduce new seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figure 2 adds CADLLM statistics and replaces annotation-preference results. For example, CADmium receives 4,893 Gemma visual-faithfulness selections in v2's pairwise comparison versus 8,387 in v3's three-way comparison, with 8,621 under Mistral. These are different comparison settings, not a same-setting performance gain. Tables 1–8 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The sphericity, curvature-difference, and Euler-characteristic definitions and equations (1)–(4) are retained. Appendix E adds conceptual explanations, not new mathematical derivations, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the annotated CAD corpus, text-to-JSON generation through fine-tuned Qwen models, structural evaluation metrics, and competitive performance claims. Added acknowledgment of the pretrained model's contribution qualifies attribution without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: Beyond v2's brief generalization and reconstruction-outlier caveats, v3 adds substantive limitations concerning absent large-scale human validation, judge and annotation-format biases, vague nonexpert prompts, and unsupported chamfer/fillet operations. Appendix E also expands explanations of annotation, evaluator, fine-tuning, and metric choices.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly discloses alternative LoRA ranks and preliminary full-fine-tuning considerations. Appendix C documents the third annotation and expanded judge-response labels, although some pairwise wording remains. Main training hyperparameters, hardware, and licensing disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations for CADFusion, CAD-Coder, CADLLM/TCADGen, and Mistral. It removes Text2CAD's characterization as the only available open-source geometrically precise annotation dataset and distinguishes expert-level datasets from less geometrically specified alternatives.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. v3 expands related-work paragraphs, adds a separate Limitations section, replaces the empty Appendix E heading with Design Choices, and updates front matter and section numbering.

P2.justification: The document adopts the TMLR presentation throughout, changing title and abstract layout, typography, headers, and table/figure placement. Figure 2 is substantially redrawn for three corpora and two judges, and Figures 11–14 update their prompt graphics. Other CAD illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: The added annotation comparator and second judge broaden validation, while Section 5 and Appendix E improve transparency about applicability, evaluation bias, and design choices. These provide a modest overall gain. Residual two-annotation wording in updated prompts and a visual-faithfulness summary insufficiently updated to reflect Figure 2 limit the reporting improvement.
